limitations: No hardware minimum, runtime or monetary cost is stated in these README sections; no cost estimate is inferred.
Checkpoint downloads, dataset bytes and transitive dependencies are not checksum-pinned by this guide. Pinning the repository does not pin those external resources.
Changing the data, embedder or Hydra settings changes the evaluation configuration; this example does not establish reproduction of a published score.
prerequisites: Git and a conda environment with Python 3.10; the README recommends this Python version.
Internet access to the official data host and the model resources selected by the configuration. Preserve the downloaded data directory structure.

steps.explanation: The clone command comes from the README; the detached checkout is added to select the exact revision reviewed here.
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/frederikkemarin/BEND.git
cd BEND
git checkout --detach ac6e80c75e09d83cf47a7b4bcf0e44599c5706cf
steps.title: Check out the reviewed code

steps.explanation: Run within the prepared Python 3.10 environment. This downloads data; it is not a small smoke test.
steps.shell:
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
python scripts/download_bend.py
steps.title: Install and download the benchmark data

steps.explanation: This is the README example verbatim; it computes two models and two tasks. Embeddings are stored as Webdataset tar.gz shards; the next step uses the gene-finding subset.
steps.title: Precompute the documented embeddings

steps.explanation: Run after gene-finding embeddings are present in data/gene_finding/<embedder>/. Task-specific Hydra configuration supplies the data, model and evaluation settings.
steps.title: Train and evaluate gene finding

summary: Run the official gene-finding downstream example using precomputed ResNetLM and AWD-LSTM embeddings. This is one BEND task, not the entire suite.
